historical_record.description: The two-story-over-basement Classical Revival firehouse of tan brick and terra cotta went up on a previously empty lot at Girard Street and Wilde Avenue, as Fire Station No. 47; "SFFD" and "No. 47" are still embossed in the medallions over the engine door.
Fire-insurance mapping showed the new Fire Station No. 47, with a hose rack along the north edge of the lot.
The station went into service as Engine Company No. 47 once its new motorized engine arrived from the maker; it had been built for motor apparatus, not horses.
The station became home to Engine Company 18, which stayed until 1973.
The station took its present name, San Francisco Fire Station No. 44.

A bond-funded expansion added a two-story contemporary wing on the north side, designed by the Department of Public Works Bureau of Architecture; the original building was seismically strengthened, renovated inside, and its engine doors replaced with a telescoping metal door.
The station was recorded on a state historic-resources form.
City planners found the station individually eligible for the California Register for its history and its architecture.
A renovation of just over $1 million, paid for by the city's earthquake-safety bond, repaired the roof, windows and brickwork and upgraded access.
The Board of Supervisors voted to start landmark designation of Fire Station No. 44.
The Historic Preservation Commission recommended Fire Station No. 44 for landmark designation after a public hearing.
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 317, San Francisco Fire Station No. 44.
